forces.title: AI for enhanced safety and operational efficiency in coal mining.
forces.description: AI and digital tools are being adopted in coal operations to improve health, safety, and environmental conditions. This includes continuous safety dashboards, autonomous vehicles, predictive analytics, real-time monitoring of worker fatigue and PPE compliance, and digital twins for simulation. Generative AI copilots analyze safety data, identify root causes, and draft incident reports, while agentic AI orchestrates preventive responses. These advancements can reduce human exposure to risks, prevent incidents, and optimize safety management in coal mining operations.
forces.source_title: Harnessing AI to make mining safer

forces.title: Geopolitical instability threatens global oil and LNG supply arteries.
forces.description: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz in 2026 significantly disrupted global oil and LNG supply, exposing the vulnerability of maritime chokepoints. This event, impacting 20% of global oil and LNG trade, demonstrates how geopolitical conflicts can lead to substantial supply shocks, price volatility, and physical damage to energy infrastructure, such as Qatari liquefaction units. Such disruptions necessitate costly rerouting, inventory drawdowns, and can trigger regional shortages, posing an ongoing risk to energy security and market stability.
forces.source_title: Aftershocks: Energy security beyond the Strait of Hormuz crisis

forces.title: Global refining system under severe stress, leading to product shortages.
forces.description: The Strait of Hormuz disruption and related damages have put the global refining system under immense pressure. Gulf refineries cut output by over a quarter, exacerbated by offline Russian capacity. Refineries in other regions struggle to replace lost output, operating at near full capacity but facing efficiency losses from suboptimal crude grades. This has led to lower yields of in-demand products like jet fuel and diesel. Product inventories are thinning, with some European and US stocks hitting five-year minimums, translating into higher refined fuel prices and potential local scarcity.
forces.source_title: Aftershocks: Energy security beyond the Strait of Hormuz crisis

forces.title: Europe rewires energy trade, reducing reliance on traditional pipeline imports.
forces.description: In response to the Strait of Hormuz crisis and broader geopolitical shifts, Europe has actively rewired its energy trade flows. The region increased seaborne oil imports while decreasing pipeline imports, particularly from Russia and Kazakhstan, diversifying its supply sources. Concurrently, the European Union announced plans for additional LNG import infrastructure, indicating a strategic shift towards more flexible and diversified gas procurement routes. This structural change aims to bolster energy security by reducing dependence on specific chokepoints and geopolitical risks.
forces.source_title: Aftershocks: Energy security beyond the Strait of Hormuz crisis

forces.title: European countries delaying coal plant retirements for energy security.
forces.description: Faced with energy security concerns, particularly from lost gas imports, some European countries are reviewing or delaying the retirement of existing coal-fired power plants. This measure aims to retain spare power generation capacity and provide a buffer against supply shocks. While increasing emissions, it highlights a short-to-medium term prioritization of energy supply reliability over decarbonization targets in specific contexts, offering a temporary tailwind to the coal and consumable fuels sector in these regions.
forces.source_title: Aftershocks: Energy security beyond the Strait of Hormuz crisis

forces.title: Norway discussing new oil and gas capacity amidst energy security drive.
forces.description: Amidst global energy security concerns, Norway is actively discussing plans for new oil and gas production capacity. This development indicates a potential increase in upstream exploration and production activity within the country. As nations seek to diversify supply and enhance energy resilience, new projects in stable producing regions like Norway represent an upside for the oil and gas upstream sector, contributing to global supply diversification and potentially boosting the country's energy exports.
forces.source_title: Aftershocks: Energy security beyond the Strait of Hormuz crisis

forces.title: Strategic petroleum reserves drawn down, prompting renewed focus on product inventories.
forces.description: Global crude oil inventories, notably the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR), were drawn down significantly to cushion the Strait of Hormuz supply shock, with the SPR reaching historical minimums. This unprecedented draw highlights the finite nature of these buffers and prompts a shift in energy security strategy. The focus is now extending to shoring up refined product reserves, which are thinner and more fragmented, indicating a structural shift towards more comprehensive inventory management across the crude and product value chain to prevent future local scarcity.
forces.source_title: Aftershocks: Energy security beyond the Strait of Hormuz crisis

forces.title: LNG buyers prioritize geographic diversification and security of supply.
forces.description: The Strait of Hormuz disruption has prompted a fundamental shift in LNG procurement, with 93% of global buyers (including 80% in Europe) prioritizing geographic diversification of supply and increased flexibility over pure cost minimization. This structural change aims to mitigate risks from geopolitical conflicts and supply chain disruptions. Companies are also seeking stronger contractual protections, particularly for force majeure clauses, delivery terms, and volume flexibility, reshaping long-term LNG supply agreements and trading practices.
forces.source_title: LNG buyers’ sentiment: Disruption and implications for procurement

forces.title: Increased investment in LNG resilience infrastructure by global buyers.
forces.description: LNG buyers are significantly increasing investments in resilience measures to manage market volatility and supply disruptions. A McKinsey survey indicates that 66% of respondents, including all in Southeast Asia and a substantial portion in Europe, are planning such investments. Key areas include storage infrastructure (30%), shipping (19%), upstream equity (17%), floating storage and regasification units (FSRUs) (15%), and regasification terminals (13%). These investments represent a significant tailwind for the LNG midstream and infrastructure segments globally, enhancing supply security.
forces.source_title: LNG buyers’ sentiment: Disruption and implications for procurement

forces.title: E&P operators insourcing capabilities and consolidating supplier base.
forces.description: There's a structural shift where major Exploration & Production (E&P) operators are increasingly building internal capabilities and insourcing functions previously outsourced to oilfield services firms. This includes developing in-house expertise and AI platforms for areas like project management, drilling, and digital analytics. Concurrently, E&P operators are concentrating spending with a smaller number of preferred suppliers, dictating terms that often transfer project risk to suppliers. This trend enhances E&P operators' control and efficiency but reshapes the traditional service provider relationship.
forces.source_title: Restoring Value Creation in Oilfield Services

forces.title: AI adoption driving productivity and efficiency in upstream E&P operations.
forces.description: The adoption of AI is becoming a significant upside driver for upstream Oil & Gas (E&P) operations, promising enhanced productivity and efficiency. Advancements include faster seismic processing, optimized maintenance strategies, and reduced nonproductive drilling time. The frontier is expanding to autonomous drilling sequences, AI-driven engineering design, and digital rehearsal of construction. These AI-enabled workflows can reshape the cost curve for E&P companies, allowing for more outcomes-based commercial models with service providers and fundamentally improving operational execution.
forces.source_title: Restoring Value Creation in Oilfield Services

viewpoints.title: Global energy system shows resilience but faces lingering vulnerabilities from major disruptions.
viewpoints.description: McKinsey observes that the global energy system, especially oil, demonstrated greater resilience than expected during the 2026 Strait of Hormuz disruption, primarily due to strategic petroleum reserves and bypass pipelines. However, this resilience has limits, with thinning inventories, stressed refining systems, and uneven impacts across regions. The disruption also exposed vulnerabilities in gas supply, with physical damage to Qatari liquefaction units expected to take years to rebuild, driving up European and Asian gas prices. Long-term energy security concerns are prompting structural shifts.
viewpoints.source_title: Aftershocks: Energy security beyond the Strait of Hormuz crisis

viewpoints.title: LNG buyers foresee structural shifts in procurement strategies due to supply disruptions.
viewpoints.description: Following the Strait of Hormuz disruption, a McKinsey survey reveals that 80% of LNG buyers expect changes in their procurement strategies, with half anticipating structural shifts. The core thesis emphasizes a move from cost minimization to prioritizing security of supply. Geographic diversification of suppliers is the top priority for 93% of respondents, including 80% in Europe, alongside increased flexibility and stronger contractual protections (e.g., force majeure clauses). This indicates a significant and lasting transformation in how LNG is sourced globally.
viewpoints.source_title: LNG buyers’ sentiment: Disruption and implications for procurement

Stability in key energy transit regions directly impacts supply continuity.

pnl_drivers.description: Price volatility driven by supply shocks and market reactions.
The ability to reroute or replace disrupted energy flows impacts operational costs and margins.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of global oil and gas supply disrupted by the Strait of Hormuz closure at its peak in 2026, relative to global combined supply. Oil accounted for 91% of this affected energy, gas for the rest.
market_sizing.source_title: Aftershocks: Energy security beyond the Strait of Hormuz crisis

new_opportunities.description: Developing new production capacities outside vulnerable regions.
Building infrastructure for alternative trade routes.
Increasing capacity for receiving liquefied natural gas to diversify gas supply.
Establishing additional strategic reserves for both crude and refined products.

market_sizing.methodology: Estimate of how much of the pre-crisis oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz could be offset by 2030 through measures underway or under discussion, in case of a future shock. This range depends on discussions translating into realized projects.
market_sizing.source_title: Aftershocks: Energy security beyond the Strait of Hormuz crisis
